Their scope is one fixed point, known uniform scalar design, fixed nuisance regularity, and exact central plateaus; the calibration application remains motivation rather than demonstrated use.

With C0=10000, every evaluation radius is at least 50000(lambda^2/4)^(-1/7), so the implemented procedure deterministically reports the full causal range whenever n≤10^18, leaving practical flat-region precision unestablished.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived the matched plateau-length envelope, constant no-log radius adaptation, and fixed-law observational premium on the unchanged model. A missing citation bibkey was repaired and independently audited without a third solve; the original Hoeffding source was attested and graph integrity verified. Mathematics passed, but specialized scope and vacuous finite-sample constants left the package at subfield tier, below the field floor; formalization was not entered.
tldr: For honest intervals for a monotone causal effect under rough observational nuisance functions, the sharp expected-length envelope is, up to universal constants, \(\rho(n,\ell)=\min\{1/2,[n^2\max\{\ell,n^{-1/4}\}]^{-1/7}\}\). One explicit original-record interval attains this order simultaneously at every unknown plateau radius, so the multiplicative adaptation cost is constant and no logarithmic penalty is necessary. At the same globally flat fair-coin observed law, full observational honesty costs order \(n^{-2/7}\), while publicly supplied randomization permits order \(n^{-1/2}\), giving an information premium of order \(n^{3/14}\).
gap: The verified literature leaves this finite-sample observational plateau-length benchmark and its unknown-radius adaptation cost undetermined. The global variance-weighted ratio in \cite{LiTchetgenTchetgenVanDerVaartRobins2011} does not determine either object.
fill: An evaluable \(L(n,\ell)\), an all-procedure converse, and one total interval attaining the sharp adaptation order would quantify that precision under the exact public primitive restrictions.
